boards.title: Your First Weekend at St Olaf College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on the Hill, finding a few campus anchors, and taking a daylight walk through the Natural Lands.

cards.title: Begin at the Information Desk
cards.subtitle: Crossroads, Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Ask for directions, current dining information, transportation schedules, or technical-support guidance before setting out around campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for campus wayfinding and current services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Information Desk is on Buntrock Commons’ ground-floor Crossroads and provides directions, dining hours, transportation schedules, and technical-support information.
cards.access_notes: The college says the desk is staffed during Buntrock building hours; confirm hours on arrival.

cards.title: Settle into Fireside Lounge
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Use this named student space for a short reset, a conversation, or to review the day’s campus plans with your group.
cards.short_summary: A documented student space inside the campus commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Buntrock Commons identifies Fireside Lounge among its student spaces and says most such spaces are intentionally unreservable to remain accessible for Oles.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to building access and any posted space rules.

cards.title: Find a calm corner in Rolvaag
cards.subtitle: East side of campus, connected to Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Walk through the library’s levels, locate its study areas, and save the service desk location for a future research question.
cards.short_summary: A campus library stop with study space and collections across multiple levels.
cards.evidence_claim: Rolvaag Memorial Library is connected to Buntrock Commons and has collections and services distributed across five and a half levels.
cards.source_title: Rolvaag Memorial Library – St. Olaf Libraries
cards.access_notes: Library hours are maintained on the library page; check them before visiting.

cards.title: See what is on view at Flaten
cards.subtitle: Main Floor, Center for Art and Dance
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition page, then make time for a gallery visit when the museum is open during your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum in the Center for Art and Dance.
cards.evidence_claim: Flaten Art Museum is on the Main Floor of the Center for Art and Dance, and its official visitor page states that admission is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit – Flaten Art Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum’s official page says galleries are closed for summer break and reopen September 11, 2026; verify current hours before going.

cards.title: Pause by Boe Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf campus
cards.notes: Add the chapel to your campus walk and consult the college calendar for public concerts, recitals, or other scheduled programs.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus performance and gathering venue.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s music site states that organ lessons are typically held in Boe Chapel on its Holtkamp Organ.
cards.access_notes: Interior access and events vary; follow posted access guidance and the college calendar.

cards.title: Spot the St. Olaf Rock
cards.subtitle: Outside Tomson Hall
cards.notes: Find the carved granite boulder outside Tomson Hall and take a quick look at a physical piece of the college’s documented history.
cards.short_summary: A named historic campus landmark near Tomson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The St. Olaf Archives identifies the St. Olaf Rock as a granite boulder outside Tomson Hall and documents its carved early representation of the college seal.
cards.source_title: Tidbits: Discovering St. Olaf: The St. Olaf Rock – College Archives
cards.access_notes: View from exterior campus walkways and respect any nearby building-access rules.

cards.title: Walk Norway Valley in daylight
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Choose a marked daylight route, stay on the trail, and take a slower look at this wooded section of the Natural Lands.
cards.short_summary: The campus’s oldest forest area, with documented native hardwoods.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies Norway Valley as a 15-acre parcel of native hardwood trees and the oldest forest area on campus.
cards.source_title: Habitats and Management of the Natural Lands
cards.access_notes: Remain on trails and follow Natural Lands rules; visit in daylight and with appropriate footwear.

cards.title: Take the Big Pond Loop
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Download or pick up the Natural Lands map, then use the suggested Big Pond Loop as a self-guided outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A mapped Natural Lands route with a college-published suggested walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Natural Lands wellness-walks page lists Big Pond Loop among its suggested walking routes, and the trail-map page provides downloadable maps.
cards.access_notes: Use the current trail map and follow Natural Lands safety and trail-use rules.

cards.title: Find Big Ole by the Art Barn
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Use the wind turbine as a visual landmark on a daylight Natural Lands walk, then continue only on mapped, permitted routes.
cards.short_summary: A named campus wind turbine beside the Natural Lands.
cards.evidence_claim: A St. Olaf page identifies the campus wind turbine as “BIG OLE” and states that the HORIZON sculpture was installed next to it in February 2023.
cards.source_title: Presenters – 2024 – Conference on Worship, Theology, and the Arts
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an outdoor landmark; do not enter restricted utility or maintenance areas.

cards.title: End with a mapped nature walk
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Finish the weekend with a route matched to your daylight, weather, and footwear; keep to trails and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: More than 430 adjacent acres for documented recreation, conservation, and education.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf says the Natural Lands encompass approximately 430 acres adjacent to campus and welcomes visitors to explore while following its safety and environmental rules.
cards.access_notes: The college asks visitors to follow Natural Lands rules; trails are open for outdoor use, with restrictions including no camping or fires.
